Solve the supplied rule-constrained task. Return short JSON matching the response schema. Jointly propose an executable rule sketch and any entity/group/usage interface. Do not omit exceptions. A compiled unit needs a source link to a binding or query; unlisted units remain residual. Do not claim unsupported text is compiled. program.kind is expression, connector, or unsupported. For expression body use bindings [{name,value,type,source}], query {op,args}, source_links {unit:[node]}. Types: integer, rational (decimal string), scalar. Connectors also accept relation {columns,rows,closed}, amounts (value,unit,owner,period,lineage,stage), allowance_bank (entries key,balance,policy,order_observable), resource_key, slot_list. Do not invent entity witnesses or guess allocation policies. A variable is {var:name}. Operators: if,and,or,not,eq,ne,lt,le,add,sub,min,max,scale (literal constant first), divide_constant (literal denominator), array,pair,object,concat. No arbitrary code. Bind observed values and rule constants from public source units. Node names are query and binding:NAME. Use unsupported with empty body when faithful executable translation is unavailable. Always give your task answer in answer; this fixed fallback has no stability certificate. Interface proposals may describe a source-linked join/group/map/reduce graph, but never use source IDs or answers as routing features. Each interfaces entry has exactly fields (allowed semantic field names), graph (connector DSL), and bindings (same source-linked binding format); use [] when unavailable. Do not store case amounts or names as reusable skill constants. Answer contract: "Entailment" or "Contradiction"
Executable contract clarification: bindings contain only extracted public inputs and rule constants; never put an answer object or a program into a scalar string. JSON text in a string is not executable. A source identifier such as s0 is provenance metadata, never a boolean or a variable. Read a bound input with {"var":"name"}. and/or/not take booleans; comparisons return booleans. Expression binding names use n_ for integer/rational, s_ for strings, b_ for booleans; numeric references must name n_ slots, string keys s_ slots, boolean references b_ slots. Choose op before writing args. The maximum expression depth is16; use concise expressions. The root query must return the native task result: a numeric operation for Airline, an if producing an Entailment/Contradiction string for SARA, and an object operation producing EC/EV for OpenExempt. OpenExempt EC values are arrays of literal legal citation strings containing §. EV values are arrays of object operations with exactly citation (a literal citation string) and claim_value (a numeric expression). if has exactly [boolean condition, complete true branch, complete false branch]; both branches must type check. add/sub/min/max/lt/le take exact numbers. scale is [literal integer, numeric expression]; divide_constant is [numeric expression, nonzero literal integer]. Arrays use {op:array,args:[...]}; pair is [string key,value expression]; object takes pair operations as its args, never raw JSON fields. source_links maps current unit IDs to existing node names: query or binding:NAME (connector:i for connectors). Use actual cited lines for each input; cite all rule/exception lines needed for the query. Every scalar string must be an exact nonempty substring of its cited unit, never a paraphrase. A boolean binding is allowed only when its cited unit explicitly contains the standalone literal true or false. Assumptions, inferred states and absent information are not boolean inputs. Express rule conditions using comparisons on quoted inputs; otherwise leave the translation unsupported. Do not mark unrelated units compiled. Omitted units remain residual. Unknown semantics must remain unsupported, never replaced with a guessed rule. Interfaces use only the seven documented connector operators, or []. The complete example below illustrates syntax using an invented task. Its answer definition and facts belong only to that invented task. Read the CURRENT public question to determine all required components of its answer. Compile the current public task afresh.
[{"public_text":"Age: 25.\nThe claim is Entailment if age is at least 21, otherwise Contradiction.","proposal":{"program":{"kind":"expression","body":{"bindings":[{"name":"n_age","type":"integer","value":25,"source":"s0"},{"name":"n_threshold","type":"integer","value":21,"source":"s1"}],"query":{"op":"if","args":[{"op":"le","args":[{"var":"n_threshold"},{"var":"n_age"}]},"Entailment","Contradiction"]},"source_links":{"s0":["query"],"s1":["query"]}}},"answer":"Entailment","compiled_units":["s0","s1"],"unsupported_units":[],"interfaces":[]}}]
The SARA task is to evaluate the exact claim supplied as query under the supplied rules and facts. Entailment means that claim follows; Contradiction means that claim is false in this binary task. The query is the proposition to classify, not an additional fact. Do not substitute another legal question.

[s0] §151. Allowance of deductions for personal exemptions
[s1] (a) Allowance of deductions
[s2] In the case of an individual, the exemptions provided by this section shall be allowed as deductions in computing taxable income.
[s3] (b) Taxpayer and spouse
[s4] An exemption of the exemption amount for the taxpayer; and an additional exemption of the exemption amount for the spouse of the taxpayer if a joint return is not made by the taxpayer and his spouse, and if the spouse, for the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins, has no gross income and is not the dependent of another taxpayer.
[s5] (c) Additional exemption for dependents
[s6] An exemption of the exemption amount for each individual who is a dependent (as defined in section 152) of the taxpayer for the taxable year.
[s7] (d) Exemption amount
[s8] For purposes of this section-
[s9]     (1) In general
[s10]     Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the term "exemption amount" means $2,000.
[s11]     (2) Exemption amount disallowed in case of certain dependents
[s12]     In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under this section is allowable to another taxpayer for a taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the individual's taxable year begins, the exemption amount applicable to such individual for such individual's taxable year shall be zero.
[s13]     (3) Phaseout
[s14]         (A) In general
[s15]         In the case of any taxpayer whose adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b), the exemption amount shall be reduced by the applicable percentage.
[s16]         (B) Applicable percentage
[s17]         For purposes of subparagraph (A), the term "applicable percentage" means 2 percentage points for each $2,500 (or fraction thereof) by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b). In the case of a married individual filing a separate return, the preceding sentence shall be applied by substituting "$1,250" for "$2,500". In no event shall the applicable percentage exceed 100 percent.
[s18]     (5) Special rules for taxable years 2018 through 2025
[s19]     In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026, the term "exemption amount" means zero.
[s20] Alice's income in 2015 is $276932. Alice is not married. The applicable amount according to section 68(b) is $250000.
[s21] Under section 151(d)(3)(B), the applicable percentage for Alice for 2015 is equal to 22.
